# Synthetic Temporal replay histories

These JSON files are compatibility baselines generated by the real time-skipping
server with production workflows and in-memory stub activities. They contain
synthetic identifiers only. No operator database, provider, Docker or credentials
are used. Normal tests replay these files and never overwrite them.

To record the initial baselines, or deliberately add histories for a new patched
workflow version:

```sh
npm run temporal:record-histories -w @space/worker
npm test -w @space/worker
```

After the initial baseline, re-recording is allowed only together with a reviewed
`patched()` workflow change. Preserve histories for older branches while adding
new ones. Never re-record a failing history to make a replay incompatibility pass.

The test-only legacy bundle selects the existing pre-patch branches without
emitting patch markers. Its recorded histories are then replayed with the
unmodified current workflow source. The negative bundle adds one timer to
`dotGoalWorkflow`; a test requires a `DeterminismViolationError`, proving the gate
can detect an incompatible change. Neither variant is used by production workers.
